precepts.text: The spirit of God came upon Zechariah to ask, Why transgress ye the commandments of the Lord, that ye cannot prosper? The moment you transgress, the prosperity is over.
precepts.point: For then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success: only after the mouth, the meditation, and the doing does prosperity follow. Thus saith God, the second you transgress the commandments of the Lord you cannot prosper, so any pastor teaching prosperity while saying the law is done away with is teaching a lie. Real prosperity never came from sowing a seed into a basket; it comes from obeying the laws of the Most High, and that applies to us as a whole nation of people.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“And the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith God, Why transgress ye the commandments of the Lord, that ye cannot prosper? because ye have forsaken the Lord, he hath also forsaken you.”

Thus saith God: the second you transgress the commandments of the Lord you cannot prosper. The moment you transgress, the prosperity is over. So any pastor teaching prosperity while saying the law is done away with is teaching a lie. Joshua was told to observe to do according to all that is written, and then he would make his way prosperous; forsake the Lord, and he forsakes you.

precepts.text: When a man keeps and meditates on the law and does it, he makes his way prosperous and has good success, which is why the willing work on the temple succeeded.
precepts.point: The workmen perfected the work and set the house of God in its state, then brought the rest of the money to make vessels of gold and silver to minister and offer with, and they offered burnt offerings continually all the days of Jehoiada.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

precepts.why:
“This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” When a man keeps the law, meditates on it and does it, he makes his way prosperous and has good success.

That is why the willing work on the temple succeeded. They brought in “the collection that Moses the servant of God laid upon Israel in the wilderness”, doing what was written, and “all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and brought in, and cast into the chest, until they had made an end.” They “gathered money in abundance”, and “the work was perfected by them, and they set the house of God in his state, and strengthened it.”

Money was a defense here, because it paid the skilled brothers who got the temple work done. Not everyone had the same task: masons, carpenters, and such as “wrought iron and brass” each had their charge, and every man had to listen to a manager, for business requires order and submission to authority. So we must deal righteously with our people today, treating a brother’s business as a place to help the family and the body. The good success came even to the rest of the money, “whereof were made vessels for the house of the Lord”, and “they offered burnt offerings in the house of the Lord continually all the days of Jehoiada.”

precepts.text: The Most High sends the prophet to turn the hearts of the fathers and children, lest He come and smite the earth with a curse; our people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.
precepts.point: As Zechariah died he said, The Most High look upon it and require it. He prayed for vengeance on his murderer, and this is scripture; it is right to pray for the downfall of enemies who do much wickedness, even while we pray for the recovery and repentance of our own people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

precepts.why:
“And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.” The Most High sends the prophet to turn the hearts of the fathers and the children, lest he come and smite the earth with a curse. Our people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.

Zechariah the son of Jehoiada was that kind of prophet: “the Spirit of God came upon” him, and he stood above the people and asked, “Why transgress ye the commandments of the Lord, that ye cannot prosper?” He came to correct the king and turn the people back.

But they “stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the Lord.” The king had him killed for telling him the truth. Joash “remembered not the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him, but slew his son.” That is the same spirit our people show today when a laborer brings the medicine and is met with violence.

precepts.text: If we seek the Most High He will be found, but if we forsake Him He will forsake us, the very charge Zechariah brought against Judah.
precepts.point: As Zechariah died he said, The Most High look upon it and require it. He prayed for vengeance on his murderer, and this is scripture; it is right to pray for the downfall of enemies who do much wickedness, even while we pray for the recovery and repentance of our own people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

precepts.why:
The prophet went out to meet Asa and said, “The Lord is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.” If we seek the Most High he will be found, but if we forsake him he will forsake us.

That is the very charge Zechariah brought against Judah: “because ye have forsaken the Lord, he hath also forsaken you.” They transgressed the commandments, so they could not prosper.

And as Zechariah died, he said, “The Lord look upon it, and require it.” He prayed for vengeance on his murderer, and this is scripture. It is right to pray for the downfall of enemies who do much wickedness, even while we pray for the recovery and repentance of our own people.

precepts.text: When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, his righteousness shall not be remembered, and he shall die in his sin, exactly as it went for Joash.
precepts.point: Amaziah his son reigned in his stead; the fuller record of Joash is written in the story of the book of the kings.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

precepts.why:
“When a righteous man doth turn from his righteousness, and commit iniquity, and I lay a stumblingblock before him, he shall die”, and “his righteousness which he hath done shall not be remembered.” He shall die in his sin. That is exactly how it went for Joash.

Joash began by doing right under Jehoiada’s guidance, repairing the house and clearing out the idols. But after he was warned he turned to wickedness and killed Zechariah, and none of that good was remembered in the end.

So judgment came: “For the army of the Syrians came with a small company of men, and the Lord delivered a very great host into their hand, because they had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers. So they executed judgment against Joash.” They left him “in great diseases”, and “his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and slew him on his bed.” He was buried “in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchres of the kings.”

points: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign and reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: Joash did that which was right in the sight of the Most High all the days of Jehoiada the priest, because that is what he was taught.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: Joash was minded to repair the house of the Most High and gathered the priests and Levites, telling them to go to the cities of Judah and gather money of all Israel to repair the house from year to year, and to hasten the matter.
Money was needed because Israel did not let the workmen labor for nothing; when men did the jobs they were paid, for the workman is worthy of his hire, and we dealt righteously with our people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: The Levites did not hasten it, so the king called Jehoiada the chief and asked why he had not required of the Levites the collection appointed by Moses for the tabernacle of witness.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: The sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God and bestowed all its dedicated things upon Baalim, which is why so much repair was needed.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: At the king's commandment they made a chest and set it at the gate of the house of the Most High, and made a proclamation to bring in the collection Moses laid upon Israel in the wilderness, and the princes and people rejoiced and cast in until they made an end.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: Day by day the king's scribe and the high priest's officer emptied the chest and gathered money in abundance, and the king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work, hiring masons, carpenters, and workers of iron and brass.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: Jehoiada waxed old and was full of days and died, being a hundred and thirty years old at his death.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: They buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel both toward the Most High and toward his house.
That a priest was buried among the kings shows how much respect and diligence this man had earned; his faithfulness set him alongside the rulers of the land.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: After the death of Jehoiada the princes of Judah came and made obeisance to the king, and the king hearkened to them.

As soon as Jehoiada died, Israel went off again, because the king was weak and started listening to those who served other gods; this teaches the lesson that lust drives Israel to idolatry, and that the Most High will always send prophets to warn them.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: They left the house of the Most High and served groves and idols, and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for their trespass.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: The Most High sent prophets to bring them again unto Him, and they testified against them, but the people would not give ear.
